newsitem.title: USA: UPS bonds deliver despite striking workers.
newsitem.headline: UPS bonds deliver despite striking workers.

text.p: Bonds of the biggest U.S. package delivery business, United Parcel Service of America Inc (UPS), remained unmoved by Monday's strike and continued to deliver steady returns, traders said.
Teamster drivers and other employees went on strike early Monday, the first company-wide strike in UPS history, after the breakdown of federally mediated contract talks.
Corporate players said the company's 8-3/8 percent bonds due 2020, which rarely trade, did not budge on the news.
"No one is looking to unload this (UPS) bond -- it's a museum piece -- a straight AAA piece of paper," said one high-grade trader.
"These bonds trade once in a while; when they do, they trade very, very tight," he said.
UPS said last week that the threat of a strike was costing it about $5 million a day in business lost to competitors such as the Postal Service and Federal Express Corp.
Meanwhile, rival shipper Federal Express has already reported a sharp pickup in business.
Seperately, on Thursday, Standard & Poor's credit rating agency affirmed UPS' AAA corporate credit and senior debt ratings and kept the outlook for the firm stable.
S&P said UPS' strong financial condition and substantial liquidity should enable it to weather a strike, which is not expected to be lengthy.
"It (UPS) is one of the very few remaining AAA credits," said John Lonski, economist at Moody's Investors Service, another major U.S. credit rating agency.

Among the few remaining higher-rated AAA names are: Exxon Corp, General Electric Co, Johnson and Johnson, Merck & Co, Bristol Meyers, Pfizer Inc, BellSouth Telecommunications, Ohio Bell, Southern Bell and Wisconsin Bell, Lonski said.
Going forward, market participants expect the bonds to continue their positive performance despite the recent news.

"I don't imagine you're going to see any affect on UPS debt," said another corporate player. "We've gone through this with Ford and Chrysler, which are lower-rated credits, and it really didn't change anybody's feelings, as far as the bonds."
Ford Motor Co senior debt is rated A1/A-plus; while Chyrsler Corp is rated A3/A by Moody's and S&P, respectively.
"If it turns out to be a protracted strike, than they may have to rethink that; but on Day One, I don't think anyone is going to care," he added.

With revenues of $22.4 billion in 1996, Atlanta-based UPS annually handles three billion parcels and documents, shipped to countries around the world; domestically, it handles 12 million packages a day.
